newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Aug kerosene output, imports stronger - MITI.
newsitem.headline: Japan Aug kerosene output, imports stronger - MITI.

text.p: Kerosene production and imports were stronger in August, helping replenish dwindling stockpiles, the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said on Thursday.
Output of kerosene, used for heating, was 2.06 million kl in August, up 20.2 percent from a year earlier and up 22.5 percent from July, MITI data showed.
Imports were 159,000 kl in August, representing a surge of 835.3 percent from a year earlier and a rise of 6.7 percent from July, MITI said.

Helped by increased output and imports, kerosene stockpiles as of end-August were 4.2 million kl, up a sharp 36.9 percent compared with the previous month, although 0.1 percent lower than the same period a year earlier, MITI said.
In other oil products, output of naphtha, used by petrochemical makers, was 1.25 million kl, down nine percent from a year earlier but up 11.8 percent from July, MITI said.
Naphtha stockpiles grew for the fourth consecutive month on a year-on-year basis by 21.2 percent to 1.9 million kl.
Production of gas oil, which is mainly used by trucks and buses for fuel, hit a record high of 4.47 million kl.
Sales of gasoline also hit a record high of 5.1 million kilolitres (kl) in August, reflecting the increasing trend in people owning cars, MITI said.
In August, gasoline sales were 1.0 percent higher compared to the same period a year earlier, and 5.3 percent above July levels, it said.
Stockpiles of gasoline decreased for the eighth consecutive month on a year-on-year basis to 1.9 million kl.
Oil industry sources said Japanese refiners are trying to keep stocks low in an attempt to tighten the demand/supply situation and help support faltering gasoline market prices.
